gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Steam Deck fast-charges only by asking for USB PD's 15 V / 3 A level and cannot use 20 V, so a power bank that offers 5 V and 20 V but no 15 V level charges it at 5 V / 15 W, whatever its total wattage.
standout_why: I opened four of the pages ChatGPT got on 2026-11-13. Three of them give only a wattage target. itechguides.com quotes Valve's '45W USB-C PD 3.0' and says to 'check the output profile for the individual port'. vgkami.com (cited) says to 'verify your handheld's preferred PD profile' but never names one. dealectric.com (our current page) says 'Valve rates both Steam Decks at 45 W USB-C PD' and nothing more. gamingonbatteries.com/best-power-bank-steam-deck (cited) covers part of it but gets it wrong: it says the Deck 'charges over USB-C PD at 5V, 9V, 15V, or 20V depending on load', which implies 20V works. None of them says that 15 V / 3 A is the one level the Deck needs, or that 20 V alone drops it to 15 W. ChatGPT's own answers repeat '65W or 100W gives headroom', which suggests wattage alone decides it.
decides: It adds a spec-sheet check rather than changing the pick. The port the Deck will use must list 15V⎓3A. A big 100 W, 140 W or 250 W total doesn't count without it. Anker's US page lists 15V⎓3A on both USB-C ports of the Anker 737 (A1289), so it passes. I couldn't open the maker pages for the INIU Cougar, UGREEN Nexode 100W, Baseus Blade H1, Anker Prime A1340 or Anker A1695 (rate-limited or 404), so they still need a 15V⎓3A line before the page can say they pass. ChargerLAB's tests also cap expectations: Valve's own 45 W adapter gave about 39 W, and about half of 10 power banks gave about 35 W, the rest 15–25 W. Telling shoppers to buy 65 W+ for headroom therefore makes no difference to the Deck.

findings.label: Steam Deck charging level and what happens without it
findings.value: Steam Deck asks for 15 V / 3 A (45 W). It cannot use 20 V. Without a 15 V level it falls back to 5 V / 15 W
findings.source_title: USB-C KVM Switch v3 (with USB Power Delivery / 135watts) does not fast-charge SteamDeck (stuck in 15W mode) - Level1Techs Forums
findings.note: Level1Techs staff (Level1_Amber), 2026-07-30: 'The Steam Deck tries to negotiate 45W / 15V charging. It cannot do standard 60W / 20V.' and 'your Steam Deck will drop down to the 5V / 15W charging as its only option.' The device offered only 5V/3A and 20V/3A per port. On 2026-08-03 staff called it 'a hardware level chipset limitation'. The device was a KVM switch, not a power bank, but the Deck's request works the same way with any USB PD source.

findings.label: Level the Deck asks for, and power from Valve's own adapter
findings.value: 15 V level; about 39 W from Valve's 45 W adapter
findings.source_title: Exploring the Charging Detail of Your Steam Deck - ChargerLAB Compatibility 100
findings.note: ChargerLAB (Joey), 2023-07-18: the Deck 'can trigger the 15V PDO, and the input power is about 39W'. None of the 80 third-party chargers tested beat 39 W.

findings.label: Power banks tested on the Steam Deck
findings.value: Of 10 power banks, most triggered 15 V; about half reached about 35 W, the rest 15–25 W
findings.source_title: Exploring the Charging Detail of Your Steam Deck - ChargerLAB Compatibility 100
findings.note: Per-model results are only in ChargerLAB's chart images, not the text, so I can't tie numbers to models. Among power stations, one gave 5 V only (no 15 V).

findings.label: Valve's stated power input
findings.value: PD3.0 Type C power supply, 45 W (Valve gives no voltage)
findings.note: Valve's spec page names neither 15 V nor 3 A. The 15 V requirement comes from ChargerLAB and Level1Techs above.

findings.label: USB-C output levels
findings.note: 15V⎓3A = 45 W, the full level the Deck asks for, on either USB-C port. The page showed 'Sold Out' and no price.
